links.outcome: Subgroup FNR/FPR gaps at selected threshold in ACTG175 mortality baseline
links.effect: Largest single-attribute FNR gap for gender (0.417); combined FPR+FNR gap 0.457; female FNR 0.750 vs male 0.333.
links.quote: The component view showed that the gender gap was mainly driven by missed mortality events: female records had an FNR of 0.750 compared with 0.333 for male records.

links.outcome: Subgroup gap reduction after mitigation with verification of balanced accuracy change
links.effect: ACTG175 gender combined gap improved by 0.190 (~55.8% relative reduction), BA +0.046; stroke aggregate gap reduction 39.41%, mean BA change −0.002, bootstrap P=0.00399.
links.quote: Aggregate combined FPR + FNR gap reduction of 39.41%; mean BA change −0.002; aggregate bootstrap P = 0.00399, so the aggregate reduction was statistically supported.

links.outcome: Whether excluding sensitive attributes removes subgroup effects via proxy variables
links.effect: Proxy signals found (age with age group, glucose/BMI); exclusion of sensitive attributes judged insufficient to remove subgroup effects.
links.quote: Another important finding is that protected-attribute removal is not a sufficient fairness strategy.
